thread:
amanda.mallory: Heads up — multiple Dedicated customers in SFO are reporting 429s + high tail latency for generation calls. ACME flagged it at 09:12. Trying to triage.
ops-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-sfo-2: 429 spike above threshold (p95 latency 1.8s -> 4.6s), 12% error rate in last 10m. Autoscaler events: failed placement attempts.
raj.patel: @oncall-sre can you take a look at autoscaler logs? Sounds like placement/stockout.
oncall-sre: Jumping in. I've pulled the autoscaler stream — seeing repeated provider errors: "InsufficientInstanceCapacity" and a few "NetworkAllocationFailure" during the window.
jessica.li: Customer-reported API response snippet: ```json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": "RequestThrottled",
  "status": 429,
  "message": "pool sfo-dedicated-2 throttled: no available GPU capacity"
}
```
marta.cs: ACME is escalated to SEV-2, they're seeing degraded product demos. They asked for ETA and whether we can fail them over to another region.
raj.patel: I tried failover to us-west-2 fallback pool, but placement there returned an error: "incompatible image flavors" — looks like our fallback variant doesn't have the same quantization/AMI. Need an infra change to accept older image at fallback.
cloud-partner-bot: Provider notice: maintenance window in sfo on 2025-02-10 02:00-06:00 UTC, limited GPU replenishment. (ID: CPX-7812) :warning:
amanda.mallory: That maintenance overlaps with our spike window. Could be depletion from previous scheduled capacity drains + autoscaler not replenishing fast enough.
oncall-sre: Autoscaler logs (excerpt):
```
[2025-02-10T09:11:33Z] scale_attempt(pool=sfo-2) -> request 8 gpus
[2025-02-10T09:11:34Z] provider_err: InsufficientInstanceCapacity: no matching instance types
[2025-02-10T09:11:34Z] backoff: exponential -> 60s
[2025-02-10T09:12:05Z] scale_attempt -> same error
[2025-02-10T09:12:40Z] placement_fail_count=6
[2025-02-10T09:13:00Z] autoscaler stuck in backoff, not trying burst-override due to policy bug #INF-462
```
raj.patel: That bug INF-462 is old — the policy prevented burst-override when provider returned capacity errors. We should have a hotfix to ignore InsufficientInstanceCapacity for override attempts.
jessica.li: Repro for customer: quick cURL to dedicated endpoint returns 429 for their API key. Example:```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/sessions/generate \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxxx' \n -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`

marta.cs: CS asked if this is billing-related (overquota) — confirmed logs show it's pool capacity throttling, not token quota. We should tell them it's infra capacity and offer failover.
amanda.mallory: Quick mitigation options: 1) emergency move high-impact customers to dedicated-us-west-2 after adjusting image compatibility; 2) temporarily increase reserved burst allotment in SFO from our reserved pool; 3) ask ACME to reduce concurrency. Which do we want?
devex: Option 1 requires image acceptance on fallback, we can patch the us-west launch config in ~30m if infra ok. Option 2 is faster but will hit cost and billing allocation.
raj.patel: I'm going to trigger emergency patch for fallback image acceptance and then trigger manual scale attempt. On it.
ops-bot: INCIDENT_NOTE: performing manual patch to fallback config (operator=raj.patel).
cloud-partner-bot: Provider update: additional GPU capacity expected in SFO in ~90 minutes, maybe partial relief.
oncall-sre: Manual scale attempt log after patch:
```
[2025-02-10T09:34:12Z] manual_scale(pool=us-west-2-fallback) -> request 6 gpus
[2025-02-10T09:34:13Z] success: instances launched
[2025-02-10T09:36:10Z] routing: moved 3 ACME tenants to us-west-2-fallback
```
jessica.li: ACME confirms reduced 429s after move, but p95 still slightly elevated (2.1s). They accepted partial failover for now. :thumbsup:
marta.cs: We told ACME we'll cover cross-region egress/burst costs for this incident. Finance ok with that for customer retention.
amanda.mallory: Root causes so far: provider maintenance + autoscaler policy bug INF-462 prevented burst override -> delayed replenishment -> pool throttling -> partial failover required. Also fallback image mismatch slowed failover.
raj.patel: Deployed hotfix to autoscaler that allows override on InsufficientInstanceCapacity, and added guard to avoid stuck backoff. Rolling out now.
oncall-sre: Patch deployed at 09:55 UTC. Metrics show autoscale retry frequency increased and placement succeeded for a few small allocations.
ops-bot: METRIC: dedicated-pool-sfo-2 error-rate dropped from 12% -> 1.4% over 20m. p95 latency trending back to baseline.
jessica.li: CS wants exact timeline and repro steps for postmortem. I'll prepare.
amanda.mallory: Postmortem assigned to @raj.patel and @jessica.li. Include customer impact, remediation, and billing decision. Target draft in 48h.
marta.cs: ACME happy with remediation notes, keeping SEV-2 until confirmed stable for 24h.
cloud-partner-bot: Provider: maintenance window completed. Additional capacity verified.
oncall-sre: Follow-ups: 1) remove INF-462 regression in autoscaler config, 2) ensure fallback images are compatible or fallback accepts image variants, 3) add an alert for "autoscaler stuck in backoff > 2m".
devex: I'll update runbook with the cURL repro and the manual fallback steps.
amanda.mallory: Thanks team — keep thread updated with any new customer reports. :white_check_mark:
